_: THE SWEEP THAT SAYS THE CITATION GATE IS RUN FROM ONE PLACE — run it from
the repository root:
cargo run -q --manifest-path tools/injection-harness/Cargo.toml -- sweep \
crates/mnemosyne-cli/sweeps/one-gate-run.sweep.json
WHAT THE CONTRACT IS. Round 1333 moved the construction of a citation-gate
run out of `cmd_validate_code_refs` and into `mnemosyne_ops::scan_citations`,
so that the agent-facing surface N295 asks for cannot grow a second one. Two
laws hold that: one names every production site that BUILDS the validator,
and one says the verdict-producing call has exactly one caller outside the
gate's own crate.
WHY THIS SWEEP EXISTS AT ALL. Both laws are text scans over tracked files,
and a text scan that reads nothing produces an empty finding list — which is
exactly what a clean tree produces. `0 red` is the shape of a law that holds
AND of a law that never looked. These injections are what tells them apart.
THE INJECTIONS COME IN TWO KINDS. Four break the WALK the law reads — its
population, its `#[cfg(test)]` skip, its type match, its caller filter's
polarity — and must redden it. Three break the THING THE LAW PROTECTS: a
second construction site, a second verdict caller, and the scope distinction
the op carries in its type.
WHAT THE FIRST RUN TAUGHT, recorded so it is not re-learned: an injection
that WEAKENS an assertion which already passes can never go red. Three of
the first seven did that — `undeclared.is_empty() || true` on a tree with no
undeclared site is green either way — and the harness reported them as
misaimed, which they were. An assertion is proven load-bearing by making the
condition it guards FALSE, never by deleting the guard.
RUN IT LOCALLY. The harness edits this tree and writes the firing record
beside this file.

injections.name: the-walk-reads-no-files
injections.why: a walk over an empty population finds no undeclared site and no second caller — the shape of a law that holds and of one that never looked, which is the whole reason this sweep exists

injections.name: a-test-module-hides-a-production-construction
injections.why: THE HOLE A TEXT SCAN COULD NOT CLOSE, now closed and held: `#[cfg(test)]` is skipped because syn is told which items carry it, not because a scan assumed the module sits last. Stop skipping and every fixture's validator reads as a production surface — the same blindness with its sign flipped, which is what makes the skip load-bearing rather than convenient. It reddens the CONSTRUCTION law only: every `scan_and_reach` a test module calls stands inside the gate's own crate, which the verdict law already filters out for being the type talking to itself

injections.name: every-struct-literal-is-the-gate
injections.why: the walk matches a struct literal by the type it names; without that check every literal in production Rust is reported as a citation gate, which is a law that finds everything and therefore says nothing

injections.name: a-second-surface-builds-its-own-gate-run
injections.why: THE THING THE LAW PROTECTS: a surface that assembles its own validator is free to disagree with every other one about which severities were in force and which store was read — the defect Rounds 1322-1324 paid for, one level up

injections.name: a-second-caller-asks-the-gate-for-a-verdict
injections.why: THE SECOND LAW'S OWN SUBJECT: another production site calling `scan_and_reach` is a second answer to `what is wrong with this tree`, free to disagree with the first about severities, store and scope — which is the whole reason Round 1333 moved the run

injections.name: the-gates-own-crate-is-counted-as-a-surface
injections.why: the filter's POLARITY: inverted, the law reads the gate's internal `scan` wrapper as the only caller and the real surface as none — a law that passes while measuring the opposite of what it says

injections.name: a-reading-of-an-unconfigured-workspace-is-an-empty-answer
injections.why: THE OTHER HALF OF THE GATE, and the same distinction one question over: `propose-implementations` exists to propose bindings, so proposing NONE because nobody configured the gate reads exactly like proposing none because the tree is fully bound. Round 1336 moved the reading into an op that answers `None` for an unconfigured workspace; collapsing that into an empty list is how the distinction Round 1141 paid for gets lost in a move

injections.name: a-scope-that-names-nothing-is-widened
injections.why: THE THING THE LAW PROTECTS, second half: `--paths` with no value is a malformed invocation, and collapsing it into `no scope` returns a clean WHOLE-TREE report for a run the caller meant to narrow. Round 1333 introduced exactly this and the behaviour test caught it, which is why the distinction now lives in the op's signature

edits.to:
Some(requested) if requested.is_empty() => None,
        Some(requested) => Some(PathScope::new(&loaded.workspace_root, requested)?),
